# `set_algo_param`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Set a named parameter of the active guide algorithm on one axis.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / established (64-bit build; 32-bit build matches (READ)) |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, guider handler @0x7ebd0 (64-bit build; 322 at 0x7eed8 after the virtual SetParam call at 0x7eec0); GetParamNames for Hysteresis @0xe25b0, Lowpass @0xe3a50, Lowpass2 @0xe4ee0, ResistSwitch @0xe6280; setters Hysteresis SetHysteresis @0xe2820, SetAggression @0xe2ac0, SetMinMove @0xe2350; Lowpass SetSlopeWeight @0xe4200, SetMinMove @0xe37f0; Lowpass2 SetAggressiveness @0xe54a0, SetMinMove @0xe4c80; ResistSwitch SetMinMove @0xe5fc0, SetAggression @0xe6d00, SetParam @0xe71f0 (fastSwitch @0xe72ec), GetParam @0xe5ea0 (no scaling) |

Selects the X or Y guide algorithm object of the mount and invokes its set-parameter operation. value is numeric; the handler returns an int (result 0 on success). Values persist per axis in the stored configuration (X and Y algorithm sections). Parameter names per algorithm (READ) are hysteresis {hysteresis, aggression, minMove}; lowpass {slopeWeight, minMove}; lowpass2 {aggressiveness, minMove}; resist-switch {aggression, fastSwitch, minMove}. minMove is in pixels (INFERRED). Limits (64-bit; 32-bit not checked; READ) are hysteresis.hysteresis 0..1; hysteresis.aggression above 0 up to 2; lowpass2.aggressiveness 0 or more, no upper limit; resist-switch.aggression above 0 up to 1 (a fraction, not scaled); resist-switch.minMove above 0; every other minMove and lowpass.slopeWeight 0 or more; fastSwitch is never rejected (non-zero means on). If the algorithm setter rejects the name or value ("invalid minMove", "invalid hysteresis", "invalid aggression", "invalid slopeWeight" or "invalid aggressiveness") the request fails (322). On an out-of-range value the setter first applies and persists a substitute (READ, 64-bit) - hysteresis.hysteresis clamped to 0 or 1; hysteresis.aggression 0.1 if not above 0, 2.0 if above 2; hysteresis.minMove 0.1; lowpass.slopeWeight 5.0; lowpass.minMove 0.2; lowpass2.minMove 0.2; lowpass2.aggressiveness keeps its live value and persists 80.0; resist-switch.aggression 1.0; resist-switch.minMove 0.1. A client should read the value back after a 322. Via the imager command port (4700) the request reaches this handler only as a forwarded unknown method; see the control service for the relay.

Side effects: Writes the active guide-algorithm parameter and its per-axis stored configuration.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"set_algo_param"`. [READ] |
| `params` | object\|array | yes | - | Object {axis, name, value} or the positional array [axis, name, value]. All three are required. No handler range, clamp or default; valid names and limits are enforced by the selected guide algorithm (rejection gives 322). Names per algorithm (READ) are hysteresis {hysteresis, aggression, minMove}; lowpass {slopeWeight, minMove}; lowpass2 {aggressiveness, minMove}; resist-switch {aggression, fastSwitch, minMove}. Limits (64-bit; 32-bit not checked; READ) are hysteresis.hysteresis 0..1; hysteresis.aggression above 0 up to 2; lowpass2.aggressiveness 0 or more, no upper limit; resist-switch.aggression above 0 up to 1 (a fraction, not scaled); resist-switch.minMove above 0; every other minMove and lowpass.slopeWeight 0 or more; fastSwitch is never rejected (non-zero means on). [READ] |
| `params.axis` | string | yes | - | Guide axis. ra and x address the X algorithm; dec and y address the Y algorithm. A non-string gives 105; behaviour for other strings is not established. [READ] |
| `params.name` | string | yes | - | Algorithm parameter name from the active algorithm's set (see the schema description). minMove is in pixels (INFERRED); resist-switch aggression is a fraction from 0 to 1 (READ). [READ] |
| `params.value` | number | yes | - | Parameter value, integer or real. A non-number gives 108; an out-of-range value is rejected by the algorithm (322) after it applies and persists a substitute value; limits in the schema description. [READ] |

Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). ## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 105 | axis or name is not a string | `expected string param` |
| 108 | value is not a number | `expected float param` |
| 322 | No guide algorithm is available, the algorithm does not know the name, or the value is out of range (a substitute value is then applied and persisted) | `could not set param` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request is not an object, is an empty object, or has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: no method of type string (a non-string method counts as missing) | `invalid request` |
| 101 | Dispatcher: text fails to parse | `invalid JSON request: <reason> on line <n> ...` |
| 103 | Dispatcher: unregistered method | `method not found` |

## Example

Request, request - Example request (values invented):

```json
{"id":49,"method":"set_algo_param","params":{"axis":"ra","name":"minMove","value":0.2}}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"set_algo_param","result":0,"code":0,"id":49}
```

Reply, error:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"set_algo_param","error":"could not set param","code":322,"id":50}
```
